t: In the churchyard of St James's Church, Piccadilly, you are looking at the Southwood Memorial, a memorial fountain. It was designed by Sir Albert Richardson, a leading English architect, teacher and writer on architecture. He was Professor of Architecture at University College London and later President of the Royal Academy. The sculpture is by Alfred Frank Hardiman, an English sculptor born in London, the son of a Holborn silversmith. The fountain is a small piece, but it brings together the work of two well-regarded figures of the early twentieth century.
